Uses of Package
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend

Packages that use io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
Package
Description
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
Code generation: turns optimized Juno IR into a complete Arduino sketch, generated assembly plus the C++ runtime shim it links against, for every supported board.
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.avr
The AVR code generator: AvrAsmBackend emits avr-gcc assembly for the ATmega4809 UNO WiFi Rev2, calling the runtime shim through generated word-interface thunks.
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.thumb2
The Thumb-2 code generator: Thumb2AsmBackend emits GNU ARM Thumb-2 assembly for the Cortex-M4 UNO R4 WiFi and the Cortex-M33 UNO Q, one generator for both cores.
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.xtensa
The Xtensa code generator: XtensaAsmBackend emits GNU Xtensa assembly for the Nano ESP32's ESP32-S3, calling the runtime shim directly through the windowed-register ABI.
  • Classes in io.github.jabrena.juno.backend used by io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
    Class
    Description
    FrameLayout
    Every value/local's fixed stack offset, and the total (8-byte-aligned) frame size to reserve.
    GeneratedCode
    What a backend generates for one program.
    IntrinsicTarget
    The instruction-set half of IntrinsicLowering: the intrinsic table says which runtime function an intrinsic calls with which argument words, and an implementation says how one such call, and the few intrinsics that touch memory directly, look in its assembly.
    ProgramLayout.DataDirectives
    The assembler directives a data section is written with: word emits 32-bit values (ARM's .word; AVR's .word is 16-bit, so it uses .long), align 4-byte-aligns, and bss switches to the zero-initialized section (AVR's assembler has no .bss shorthand).
    WordSource
    One argument word of a call: Juno's calling convention passes every argument as 32-bit words, in order.
